Rashi on Shabbat 82a:10:1.hebrew: שפיר קאמר ר' יוסי - דמדלייט לה בה, ש"מ דחזי:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:10:1.english: Rabbi Yosei spoke well - For since [the prophet] curses them with it, learn from this that it is fit [for use].

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:10:2.hebrew: אפילו מידי דלא חשיב - כגון לחשוף מים, לא לישתכח בה. ולעולם, לא חשיב שיעורא אלא לחתות אור:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:10:2.english: Even an item that is not significant - Such as [a potsherd] to scoop water shall not be found in it. And in truth, a measure is not considered [significant] except [one large enough] to stoke a fire.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבי עקיבא מניין לעבודה זרה כו' - משום דבעי למיתני בהדייהו "מניין שמרחיצין את המילה", כייל להו להנך דדמיין לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:12:1.english: Rabbi Akiva said: From where [is it derived] that idolatry, etc. - Because [the Tanna] wanted to teach alongside them [the laws of Shabbat]: “From where [is it derived] that one may wash the circumcision,” he grouped together those [teachings] that resemble it.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:12:2.english: By carrying - [It defiles] a person who carries it.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:12:3.english: You will cast them away like a menstruating woman, etc. - [The verse] is speaking of idolatry.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:13:1.english: His wall was adjacent to [a house of] idolatry - That that wall was a partition also for the house of idolatry.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:13:2.english: It is prohibited to rebuild it - For he benefits idolatry.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:1:1.english: That you do not wipe with an earthenware shard - [So] that I would be able to perform witchcraft against you.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:1:2.english: And you do not kill a louse on your garments - And you do not kill a louse on your garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:1:3.hebrew: ולא אכיל לכו ירקא מכישא דאסר גינאה - אין אתם מוציאין שום וכרישא ובצל מאגודה שאוגדין הגננים ואוכלים, אלא אתם מתירין האגודה תחילה. ש"מ, כל הני קשה לכשפים:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:1:3.english: And you do not eat vegetables from a bundle tied by the gardener - You do not remove garlic, leeks, and onions from a bundle that gardeners tie and eat [them], but rather you untie the bundle first. Learn from this: all of these [practices] make one vulnerable to witchcraft.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:1.hebrew: מותיב לי במילי דעלמא - מושיבני לפניו בדברי חנם, שאינו תורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:1.english: He sits me down in mundane matters - He seats me before him in idle matters, which are not Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:2.hebrew: לא ליתיב בהדיא - במהרה ובחוזק, לפי שנפתח הנקב בחזקה, וניתקין שיני הכרכשא ויוצאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:2.english: He should not sit down abruptly - Quickly and forcefully, because the orifice opens forcefully, and the teeth of the rectum are torn loose and it prolapses.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:3.hebrew: ולא ליטרח טפי - פדיימבר"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:2:3.english: And should not exert [himself] excessively - Prembre in Old French [meaning to press or strain].

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:3:1.hebrew: מקנח בצרור - בשבת, אע"פ דלאו בר טלטול הוא בעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:3:1.english: Wipes with the stone - On Shabbat, even though it is generally not permitted to be handled.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:3:2.english: And he does not wipe with an earthenware shard - Because of danger.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:3:3.english: He wipes with the earthenware shard - For it has the status of a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:3:4.english: With the rims of vessels - For they are smooth and do not tear the flesh.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:1.hebrew: ואינו מקנח בעשבים - שהעשבים לחים וחותכין את הבשר. ורבותינו מפרשים: משום תלישה. ואיני יודע מהו, דאי בעשבים מחוברין — מי איכא מאן דשרי? וכמדומה אני דמוקמי לה במחוברין, ומקנח בהן בחיבורן:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:1.english: And does not wipe with grasses - Because the grasses are moist and cut the flesh. And our teachers explain: Because of detaching [them on Shabbat]. And I do not understand this [explanation], for if [it refers] to attached grasses, is there anyone who permits [it]? And it seems to me that they establish it with attached [grasses], where he wipes with them while they are attached.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:2.hebrew: ואינו מקנח בצרור - דלאו בר טלטול הוא. הלכך, מקנח בעשבים כשהן במחובר, ולא יזיזם. ומשום שימוש במחובר לא מיתסר, כדאמרי' בעירובין בפרק ג' (דף לד:) דלא אסרו אלא באילן ובקנים עוזרדין, לפי שהן קשין:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:2.english: And he does not wipe with the stone - For it is not [an item] fit to be handled [on Shabbat]. Therefore, he wipes with the grasses while they are attached [to the ground], and he must not move them. And it is not forbidden on account of using [something] attached [to the ground], as we say in Eruvin in the third chapter (34b), that they forbade [this] only with a tree and with hardened reeds, because they are rigid.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:3.english: His teeth fall out - The teeth of the mouth [fall out] on account of the rectum.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:4:4.english: Moist [grasses] - Fire does not take hold of it.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:5:1.hebrew: רוח רעה - ריח הפה, שהזבל מרקב במעיים ויוצא ריח דרך פיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:5:1.english: An evil spirit - Bad breath; for the waste rots in the intestines, and an odor exits through his mouth.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:5:2.hebrew: רוח זוהמא - כל גופו מסריח בזיעה מסרחת, שהריח נבלע בבשרו ובאבריו, והוה בו לזיעה מזוהמת:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:5:2.english: An odor of filth - His entire body stinks with foul sweat, as the odor is absorbed into his flesh and his limbs, and becomes foul perspiration in him.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:6:1.english: And is unable to relieve himself - For the orifice does not open.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:6:2.hebrew: יסתלק לצדדין - כשבדק עצמו בזוית זו, יסתלק לזוית אחרת ויבדוק:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:6:2.english: He should move to the sides - When he has checked himself in this corner, he should move to another corner and check [again].

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:7:1.english: One who enters a regular meal - And it is disgraceful for him if he has to get up from the meal and relieve himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:7:2.hebrew: י' פעמים - ימתין בין פעם לפעם, ויבדוק עצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:7:2.english: Ten times - He should wait between one time and the next, and check himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:7:3.hebrew: ואמרי לה ד' פעמים של י' י' - דהכי עדיף טפי, שהילוך מרובה מוריד הזבל לנקביו:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:7:3.english: And some say, four times of ten [cubits each] - For this is even better, as walking a greater distance brings down the waste to his orifices.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:1.hebrew: בין פצים לחברו - כשמסדרין פצימין ועמודים וקורות, ועושין סואר של קורות על הארץ, ויש חלל בין זה לזה — סומכן מתחתיו שלא יתעקם:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:1.english: Between [one] post and another - When arranging posts, pillars, and beams, and making a stack of beams on the ground, and there is a space between one and the other, one supports them from underneath so that it will not bend:

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:2.english: An allusion to the matter - That a shard is considered significant for stoking fire.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:3.hebrew: לחשוף - לדלות. וחבירו: "חשפי שובל" (ישעיהו מז) — חשפי מים שעל הנתיבה, שתצטרכי לעבור הגשמים ושריעת נהרות:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:3.english: To extract - To draw [water]. And its counterpart [in Scripture is]: “Uncover the train” (Isaiah 47:2) — [meaning,] scoop away the water that is upon the path, as you will need to cross the rains and the overflow of rivers.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:8:4.english: From a cistern - A pit in which water collects.

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:9:1.hebrew: מסתברא שיעורא דרבי יוסי נפיש ומקרא שיעורא דר' מאיר נפיש - אתקפתא היא. כלומר: לפי דבריהם נראה שרבי מאיר מחמיר, דאמר "לחתות בו אור" ולא פי' שיעורא, וחרס פורתא חזי לחדא גחלת, ואילו לקבל רביעית מים נפיש שיעורא. וכי מעיינת בקרא — לחשוף מים זוטר; דאי ס"ד לחשוף מים נפיש, לייט לה שלא יותר בה אפילו כלי קטן, והדר אמר כלי גדול?! וכי דרך המקללים כן:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:9:1.english: It is reasonable [to say that] the measure of Rabbi Yosei is greater, but from the verse the measure of Rabbi Meir is greater - This is an objection. That is to say: according to their words [in the Mishnah], it appears that Rabbi Meir is more stringent, for he said "to rake fire with it" and did not specify a measure, and a tiny shard is suitable for a single coal; whereas to hold a revi'it of water is a greater measure. But when you examine the verse, [to] scoop water is smaller; for if it could enter your mind that [to] scoop water is greater, would [the prophet] curse it [by saying] that not even a small vessel should remain of it, and then say a large vessel?! Is that the way of those who curse?!

Rashi on Shabbat 82a:9:2.hebrew: אמר אביי מתני' - דקאמר רבי מאיר לחתות אור, מיקידה גדולה קאמר — שאפילו גחלת קטנה אינו ראוי לחתות בה אלא בחרס גדול, מפני שהוא נכוה:
Rashi on Shabbat 82a:9:2.english: Abaye said: The Mishnah - When Rabbi Meir said "to stoke fire," he meant from a large conflagration — for even [for] a small coal, it is not suitable to rake in it except with a large shard, because one would be burned.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבי עקיבא מניין לע"ז כו' - פי' בקונטרס: דנקט לה הכא משום דבעי למיתני "מנין שמרחיצין את הקטן". ואין נראה, דא"כ, בההוא הוה ליה להתחיל; ועוד, דהוה ליה למתנייה בפרק רבי אליעזר דמילה. אלא נראה: אגב דתנא לעיל בסוף "המוציא" קראי דאסמכתא גבי חרס, נקט נמי הני קראי דאסמכתא; וקרא ד"תזרם" כו' הוא סמוך לההיא קראי דאייתי לעיל: "לא ימצא במכיתתו חרש" וגו':
Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:12:1.english: Rabbi Akiva said: From where [is it derived that] idolatry, etc. - Rashi explains that [the Tanna] taught this here because he wanted to teach: "From where [is it derived] that one washes a child [on Shabbat]?" And this does not appear [correct], for if so, he should have begun with that [teaching]! And furthermore, he should have taught it in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Eliezer of Circumcision"! Rather, it appears: Since [the Tanna] taught above at the end of [the chapter entitled] "HaMotzi" verses of asmakhta [scriptural support] regarding a potsherd, he also cited these verses of asmakhta; and the verse "You will cast them away..." etc., is adjacent to that verse which was cited above: "There shall not be found in its shattered pieces a sherd..." etc.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:13:1.hebrew: אסור לבנותו - אפילו למ"ד בפרק קמא דמס' ע"ז (דף יג.): נהנה אסור, מהנה מותר — ה"מ לגבי מכס, שאין נראה כל כך לע"ז כוונתו, אלא שנותן כדי שיניחוהו לעבור; אבל הכא, נראה כאילו בונה לה בית. ר"י:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:13:1.english: It is prohibited to rebuild it - Even according to the one who says in the first chapter of tractate Avodah Zarah (13a) [that] deriving benefit is prohibited [but] providing benefit is permitted — this applies [only] regarding customs duty, where his intention is not so apparent [to be] for idolatry, but rather he gives [the toll] so that they allow him to pass; but here, it appears as though he is building a house for it. — [The] Ri.

Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:13:2.hebrew: כונס לתוך שלו ד"א - במסכת ע"ז פריך עלה: "והא שביק רווחא לעבודה זרה?" ומשני לה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 82a:13:2.english: He moves four cubits into his own [land] - In tractate Avodah Zarah, [the Gemara] challenges this: "Doesn't he leave an open space for idolatry?" And it resolves it.
